end.summary:
• Company’s progression from trading to ruling was practised: Zoya ordered 1600, Plassey, Buxar and Crown rule in 1858; a why/new-situation check is still needed.
• Revenue rights, armies, alliances and battles were practised; some links were right but the methods are not steady yet.
• Responses to colonial rule, including peasant hardship, indigo cultivation and Champaran, were practised; a why/new-situation check is still needed.
• Comparing colonial sources was practised; Zoya identified different viewpoints and evidence types, but source interpretation is not steady yet.
end.parentNote: Asha practised the Company’s shift from trade to rule, including Plassey, Buxar, revenue collection and the use of income to fund trade and armies. Zoya also practised explaining pressure on weavers and farmers, indigo cultivation, and Champaran; using cause-and-effect examples helped. When comparing sources, they identified the official and Naoroji perspectives and suggested checking records, tax figures and famine data, but their final answer still treated increased trade as possible support for the Company’s claim, so this mix-up was not corrected after the last example. At home, ask Zoya to compare one colonial-era source with one critic’s source and name the claim, evidence and viewpoint in each.

British officials sometimes called colonial rule progress, while Indian critics described losses. Why might those two accounts disagree, and how would tum judge them?

Matlab, British waala keh raha hai unhone order laaya, trains, schools, sab theek kiya. Aur Naoroji keh rahe hain ki India ka paisa Britain ja raha hai. Dono alag baat kar rahe hain, ek positive side, ek negative. Historian shayad... pata nahi, dono padhke dekh sakta hai kaun sahi hai.

Tumne dono claims pakde: the official points to order and trains, while Naoroji points to money leaving India. For a historian, reading both is a start; they also need evidence to test each claim. What kind of record might show whether wealth was leaving India?

Wo dono apni apni side se bol rahe the na – ek sarkar ke liye kaam karta tha, doosra dekhta tha ki paisa kahan ja raha hai. Historian trade records, tax figures, famine data vagera compare karega, jaise Naoroji ne kiya.

Haan, tumne dono ke viewpoints aur trade records, tax figures, famine data jaise evidence bataye. Agar trade records dikhayen ki India se bahut maal gaya, par badle mein kam paisa aaya, kis writer ki baat ko zyada support milega?
Pata nahi madam... agar maal gaya toh shayad Company wala sahi keh raha hoga ki trade badh raha hai?

Tum soch rahi ho ki zyada maal bhejna matlab trade badhna, isliye official sahi hoga. Par maal jaane aur uske badle paisa milne mein farq hai. Agar India se kapda gaya aur uske badle bahut kam paisa aaya, kiski baat ko support milega: official ki ya Naoroji ki?
